author: Codex /root; independent question-by-question assessment
changeNote: Initial complete assessment using this project’s 240 questions. Representative egalitarian-liberal feminist inferences are distinguished from explicit programme commitments; no imported scores. Contemporary acts are contextual evidence, not a profile of an incumbent government.

metadata.name: Liberal feminism
metadata.description: American egalitarian liberal feminism, emphasizing equal rights, personal autonomy and public support for equal opportunity; represented by NOW and liberal feminist scholarship.
metadata.scope: Egalitarian liberal feminism in the United States, with NOW as a programme example and liberal feminist scholarship as the theoretical boundary. Excludes libertarian equity feminism and socialist feminism. Contemporary government measures illustrate compatible policies without making any government representative of the whole doctrine. Non-core policy questions are explicitly modelled applications of autonomy, equal citizenship and institutional pluralism, not claims that every adherent takes these positions.
metadata.phrase: A society securing equal civil rights, political participation and practical opportunities for women through legal and institutional reform.

sources.title: NOW’s Principles for Comprehensive Immigration Reform
Paid Parental Leave to expand to 6 months

axes.brief: Equal political agency requires competitive elections, inclusive suffrage and constitutional accountability (now; fem). Referendums and recalls remain subject to minority rights.
axes.counterEvidence: NOW criticises particular court judgments and advocates constitutional amendment (resolutions); that is not rejection of independent constitutional review. Direct-democracy mechanisms are conditional inferences.

answers.rationale: Regular competitive elections make women equal co-authors of government rather than subjects of permanent rulers.
Expert advice is useful, but substituting an expert panel for citizens denies equal political agency.
Intellectual or educational exclusions would contradict equal citizenship and reproduce unequal opportunities.
Constitutional lawmaking and congressional accountability rule out unilateral executive legislation against parliament.
Competitive opposition is necessary for meaningful and inclusive electoral choice.
Legislative scrutiny of public spending enables accountability for priorities affecting care and equality.
The constitutional civil-rights strategy requires courts able to remedy unlawful governmental decisions.
Union representation cannot replace the equal political voice of citizens outside organised labour.
Government exclusion of opponents by political position undermines equal participation and competitive choice.
Binding popular repeal is supported as participation, inferred subject to constitutional equality protections.
The demand for legislative control of executive action contradicts sole national decision authority.
The contemporary programme expressly favours impeachment or resignation as constitutional accountability mechanisms.
A leader deciding when voters may judge them destroys accountable co-authorship of government.
Defined recall procedures can extend voter accountability, provided equal participation and due process are preserved.
Unaccountable national leadership directly denies citizens political autonomy.
Military replacement of civilian government bypasses the constitutional democratic processes used to secure equal rights.

axes.brief: Personal autonomy and bodily choice support civil liberties; protection against violence permits proportionate court-supervised intervention (fem; issues).
axes.counterEvidence: Anti-violence policy is not unrestricted police discretion. Current NOW resolutions explicitly oppose policing without reasonable suspicion and denial of due process. Firearms and drug policy answers are applications, not quoted organisational rules.

answers.rationale: Self-regarding adult choices belong to personal autonomy; support is qualified because addiction can undermine effective choice.
Court-authorised investigation of serious violence can protect autonomy while checking intrusive state power.
Peaceful collective protest is a means of equal political participation; temporary disruption with emergency access is proportionate.
Offence alone cannot justify silencing criticism of the institutions governing citizens.
Paternalistic restrictions primarily protecting competent adults conflict with bodily self-determination.
Long-term tracking without suspicion exceeds the targeted protection compatible with privacy and due process.
A limited intoxication test protects other road users against concrete harm, unlike policing purely self-regarding conduct.
A court finding serious danger can justify proportionate preventive protection for potential victims.
Government moral disapproval does not override adults’ freedom to form their own views and lives.
Private communication without universal state identification supports autonomy, association and safety from coercive exposure.
The opposition to searches without reasonable suspicion favours individualised grounds even in a threatened area.
A credible danger creates a genuine balance: protect peaceful assembly while permitting narrowly necessary measures against serious violence.
A judicial warrant with an immediate-safety exception combines privacy with protection against violence.
Disclosure of official misconduct serves accountability; the inference preserves safeguards for victims’ identifying information.
Self-defence and reducing violence are both autonomy interests; a violence-history check alone does not settle their balance.
Indefinite detention without independent review contradicts the programme’s explicit due-process commitments.

axes.brief: Equal citizenship accommodates cultural difference while rejecting practices that subordinate women (immigration; fem). National belonging need not require cultural uniformity.
axes.counterEvidence: The egalitarian tradition protects an individual’s ability to leave or contest cultural practices. Neither the national majority nor a minority community has an automatic right to impose its customs.

answers.rationale: Equal autonomy judges conflicting practices by their effects on persons, not automatic national-cultural priority.
Culturally and linguistically competent services can make access substantive, even when accommodation costs money.
Equal participation does not require adopting every majority custom; basic civic rights and responsibilities still apply.
Integration into civic life is compatible with retaining a foreign cultural identity.
The programme calls for linguistically competent care rather than allowing one-language provision to exclude migrants.
Acknowledging Indigenous people follows inclusive civic recognition rather than ranking groups by their size.
Equal cultural standing weighs against funding predominately by majority status.
Minority identity deserves protection but cannot automatically override common equal-rights obligations; neither blanket priority is accepted.
Reasonable scheduling accommodation can preserve equal participation without abandoning all common arrangements.
Recognition of several traditions expresses equal belonging among women of different backgrounds.
The programme seeks full economic and political participation; this supports integration without forced cultural renunciation.
Accessible local information can require migrant languages, inferred from linguistically competent public services.
Families’ cultural identification should remain a personal choice rather than a prescribed national hierarchy.
Voluntary religious dress merits accommodation, but a blanket exception to otherwise justified safety restrictions would require a proportionality assessment.
A plural national identity is consistent with equal inclusion across race, ethnicity and religion.
Support for integration concerns access and equal rights rather than replacing distinct community customs.

axes.brief: NOW’s immigration principles favour regularisation, family unity, independent status and access to services, including for undocumented women.
axes.counterEvidence: Support for fair legal entry and residence is not an explicit abolition of all border rules. Numerical caps, graduate routes and cultural diversity as a selection criterion are reasoned applications. Safe harbour and regularisation support durable inclusion, but do not directly establish permanent residence for every refugee.

answers.rationale: A strict cap determined only by housing and labour deficits would neglect family unity and protection needs.
Accessible lawful residence and work routes fit the programme’s concern for migrant opportunity and dignity.
Skills-only admission would exclude family members and care workers whose inclusion the programme expressly seeks.
Improving family reunification directly supports joining settled partners and dependent children.

The combination of safe harbour for threatened women and pathways to residence supports durable refugee inclusion beyond skills or cultural fit; permanent status for every refugee is an inference, not an explicit universal promise.
The explicit legalisation programme supports allowing undocumented residents to remain through a fair regularisation route.
Employer demand should neither control admission nor be ignored; independent migrant rights and public capacity require a balanced decision.
Housing pressure and migrants’ equal opportunity both matter; adequate service investment and entry arrangements must be considered together.
Family reunification is a distinct human interest and should not simply be displaced by employment-based quotas.
Work permits and pathways to residence support accessible labour migration with enforceable worker rights.
Mandatory dependence on an employer or relative can trap women in exploitation, contrary to independent status.
Education can reasonably support a residence route, while graduation alone need not override other fair eligibility conditions.
Safe harbour for persecution and violence should not disappear when ordinary admissions quotas are exhausted.
Preference by cultural similarity conflicts with equal treatment across ethnic and religious backgrounds.
Healthcare and safety-net access regardless of status directly support extending basic welfare access to migrants.
Cultural diversity is compatible with inclusion, but difference alone is neither a reason to admit nor to exclude a person.

axes.brief: Contemporary NOW resolutions give diplomacy, civilian protection and peace priority, while distinguishing aggression from a credible immediate threat.
axes.counterEvidence: This variant is not absolute pacifism: the resolution rejects wars without credible immediate danger rather than all defensive force. Military equality for women does not imply support for larger warfighting capacity.

answers.rationale: Force for interests without an immediate threat conflicts with the programme’s opposition to aggression.
The foreign-policy resolution explicitly prioritises diplomacy, conflict resolution and peacebuilding.
Redirecting resources toward communities weighs against paying for superiority as an independent national aim.
The resolution distinguishes an evidenced immediate threat from unsubstantiated aggression, permitting narrowly defensive prevention.
Defence against attack is legitimate, but the resolution also recognises immediate threats before an attack; the absolute restriction is too narrow.
Male-only compulsory service imposes a sex-assigned civic burden and expands militarisation.
Substantial diplomatic concessions can be justified to protect civilians and prevent war, subject to basic rights.
Removing human attack approval raises accountability and civilian-protection concerns that efficiency alone does not resolve.
Defensive protection better fits the emphasis on immediate danger than discretionary foreign campaigns.
Avoidance at all costs could abandon people under attack; the programme’s anti-aggression position is not unconditional non-resistance.
Permanent expeditionary capacity diverts resources toward the militarism the programme opposes.
Peaceful continuation of a territorial dispute is preferable to initiating war over it.
Coercive threats can endanger civilians and displace the preferred diplomatic resolution of disputes.
Reducing war risk is the stronger priority where displays of resolve undermine peace.
Intelligence protecting against an immediate threat can be justified; seeking advantage at the cost of escalation is not a general mandate.
Negotiated capability reductions are consistent with peacebuilding if they preserve adequate protection against aggression.

axes.brief: Universal human rights and cross-border solidarity favour international cooperation, especially on women’s rights (now; resolutions).
axes.counterEvidence: International cooperation does not itself commit this doctrine to a monetary union or political federation. Institutional legitimacy and individual rights constrain both domestic and international authorities.

answers.rationale: Domestic finality should not immunise violations of internationally recognised human rights.
Accepted international standards can constrain a government even when its present leadership objects.
Rights-based international adjudication should not be defeated automatically by contrary domestic law.
Durable cooperation can require reciprocal limits on unilateral freedom, particularly for peace and rights.
Democratic consent supports withdrawal, while obligations to other people limit unilateral escape; the procedure depends on the commitment.
Accountability for officials is consistent with universal rights and should extend to agreed international adjudication.
Human rights are indivisible across borders, so national advantage does not automatically override common goals.
Shared authority can address cross-border environmental harms affecting equal life opportunities.
A common rights-respecting foreign policy can support collective peace efforts; independence is not sufficient reason for exclusion.
International requirements protecting equal rights can legitimately require domestic legal reform.
National and shared currencies can both serve autonomy and fair distribution; the institutional design and social effects decide.
Pooling resources for shared problems follows the international dimension of equal rights and human welfare.
Protection obligations and migrant rights justify some shared constraints on exclusive border authority.
Negotiated common rules can make cross-border exchange accountable and predictable, provided equal rights are protected.
A federation and a sovereign democracy can each secure equal political agency; neither institutional scale is intrinsically preferred.
Cooperation in enforcing agreed rights and peace rules can outweigh immediate national advantage, without endorsing every military enforcement proposal.

axes.brief: This reformist doctrine seeks equal opportunity within an economy containing both private enterprise and public services; ownership is an instrument, not the ultimate criterion (now; fem).
axes.counterEvidence: NOW supports public care infrastructure (resolutions), but that does not mandate nationalising banks, rail, mining or broadcasting. Conditional neutrals here express institutional pluralism, not fabricated ownership commitments.

answers.rationale: Equal access to business and professions within a reformed market economy supports a substantial private business sector.
Public utility ownership and regulated private provision can both secure equal access; control, affordability and accountability determine the choice.
Equal cost and access leave autonomy and accountability relevant; the doctrine gives neither ownership form automatic preference.
A public competitor can remedy exclusion, but establishing one is not intrinsically better than effective regulation and equal access.
Affordable reproductive and general healthcare can use either ownership model; a general private-ownership preference does not follow.
Public rail infrastructure and regulated private infrastructure can both expand opportunity; access and accountability matter more than network title alone.
A lower-cost provider with equal quality and access can preserve resources for autonomy-enhancing services, conditional on fair labour standards.
A public bank could widen credit access, while anti-discrimination and regulation can do so through private banks; the choice is instrumental.
Selling commercial firms may fund equality measures or reduce useful public capacity; support for public care does not itself determine commercial ownership.
Housing equity and survivor security can be pursued through public ownership, regulated private rental or financial assistance; the programme does not privilege a substantial public title share.
Security regulation addresses one interest, while equal access and accountability still determine whether private ownership is suitable.
Resource ownership is judged by fair benefits and environmental costs rather than a categorical public or private presumption.
Municipal operation and private waste contracts can both satisfy equal service and worker protections; ownership alone does not settle the issue.
Strategic retention can protect access, while a sale can fund equal opportunity; the balance depends on what public control actually secures.
Subsidy needs alone do not establish failure or a case for sale when a service supplies public benefits that markets underprovide.
A plural media system with an independent public broadcaster can widen political voice beyond commercial purchasing power.

axes.brief: An open economy is acceptable when exchange preserves labour rights and equal opportunities. Neither national business protection nor trade liberalisation is an unconditional feminist end (fem; immigration).
axes.counterEvidence: The immigration programme’s worker protections constrain cost-only arguments. These trade responses are explicit applications of egalitarian liberalism, not an attributed NOW tariff schedule.

answers.rationale: Protecting firms solely from competition is weaker justification than remedying demonstrable unequal opportunity.
Open exchange can expand opportunity despite particular firms losing sales, with adjustment support and labour safeguards.
Lower prices support service budgets, while labour and equality conditions can justify procurement preferences; origin alone is insufficient.
Commercial choice is generally compatible with autonomy, constrained by worker rights rather than a domestic-origin rule.
Essential supply resilience and affordable access both matter; their trade-off requires evidence rather than a categorical import restriction.
Unilateral openness can benefit consumers but may undermine reciprocal social safeguards; the distribution of gains matters.
An infant-industry measure can expand opportunity yet raise living costs; its equality effects determine whether it is justified.
Equal terms for foreign and domestic investors fit non-discrimination under common social regulation.
Food security and affordable food are competing public interests; domestic farming is not an overriding end in itself.
Adjustment with worker support is normally preferable to sheltering firms merely because they face competition.
Retaliation may sustain fair rules but also burdens consumers; it is a contingent tool, not an automatic obligation.
Like products generally deserve common taxes; legitimate social standards should apply without arbitrary origin discrimination.
Correcting subsidy distortion can be justified, but only alongside consideration of consumer affordability and worker effects.
Negotiated tariff reduction is compatible with mutual opportunity if dependence does not undermine essential access and labour rights.
Strategic control may protect public interests; foreign ownership itself is not evidence that equal access or accountability will suffer.
Access to foreign online services supports individual choice, subject to ordinary privacy, equality and consumer protections.

axes.brief: Egalitarian liberal feminism accepts markets while using regulation, care investment and labour standards to sustain substantive freedom. NOW currently supports minimum-wage increases and rent control.
axes.counterEvidence: A welfare state is distinct from compulsory production planning. Neutral financial-policy responses balance effective public capacity against decentralised choice, rather than treating redistribution as proof of central planning.

answers.rationale: Independent firms and professional opportunities are compatible with equality under enforceable social rules.
Compulsory industrial output targets extend beyond the targeted measures needed for equal opportunity.
Market prices can coordinate ordinary exchange, while essential access remains subject to corrective regulation.
Directed investment in care and education can correct structural barriers that private investment leaves in place.
Demand-responsive business decisions are generally compatible with a reformed market economy, alongside worker transition protections.
Controls can be justified for essential access; the explicit rent-control commitment illustrates willingness to constrain suppliers’ prices.
Business entry should remain open under common standards rather than require proof of a planning authority’s output need.
Targeted credit can remedy exclusion, but political allocation may reproduce it; autonomy and fair access make the instrument conditional.
Cross-border financial choice is generally acceptable with tax, anti-exploitation and consumer-protection obligations.
Public support for care and other neglected social needs can legitimately redirect development beyond private returns.
Currency experimentation and monetary stability are competing autonomy interests; permission depends on regulation and actual access effects.
The contemporary programme explicitly advocates raising the legal minimum wage.
Negotiated wages can coexist with minimum standards and equal-pay law without comprehensive state wage schedules.
Employment and care investment matter, but subordinating all monetary decisions to a plan is not entailed; accountable institutional design decides.
NOW’s explicit support for rent control contradicts leaving rental prices entirely to market demand.
Targeted equality interventions do not require routine state coordination of all national production and distribution.

axes.brief: Autonomy requires material resources, care support and a fair distribution of opportunities. NOW’s current economic programme supports basic income and public care; Australia’s 2026 leave expansion is a compatible incumbent-government example.
axes.counterEvidence: Support is for meaningful resources and fair opportunity, not identical incomes. The Australian release is corroboration of a policy instrument, not evidence that NOW endorsed that government or every detail of its scheme.

answers.rationale: Reducing large disposable-income inequalities can make formal freedom and political participation practically usable.
Unequal resources can undermine equal autonomy, so reducing inequality can itself supply a public justification for taxation.
A stronger income floor protects independence and participation, even when collective funding requires higher taxes.
Survival alone does not secure the resources needed for meaningful choice and equal citizenship.
Progressive taxation is a defensible way to fund equal opportunity while distributing burdens by ability to pay.
The programme opposes tax priorities benefiting wealth at the expense of care and low-income households.
Taxing large inheritances can reduce unearned starting inequalities and fund autonomy for people with fewer resources.
Time limits that leave people without adequate means conflict with income security and recognition of care barriers.
Transfers funded from concentrated wealth are compatible with the programme’s distributive and anti-poverty priorities.
Taxpayer savings are not sufficient reason to keep support below the level required for effective independence.
Equal citizenship requires resources for ordinary participation, not merely physical survival.
The current economic agenda favours benefits and care investment over further tax cuts for the wealthy.
Income supplements can improve material independence for low-paid workers; public leave payments illustrate support beyond wages alone.
Uniform marginal taxation is not required where progressive contributions fairly finance equal opportunity.
Fair opportunity can justify compensated land reform, but redistribution in cash or services may serve it better; land concentration alone is not decisive.
Autonomy and caregiving support can extend beyond destitution; the incumbent Australian leave scheme illustrates broader eligibility.

axes.brief: Equal personal autonomy, reproductive freedom and plural citizenship support civil government independent of religious authority (fem; issues; resolutions).
axes.counterEvidence: Religious women and voluntary religious practice are included. Opposition is to governmental privilege and compulsory authority, not to personal belief or cultural celebration.

answers.rationale: Equal citizens need public justifications they can assess without adopting a particular faith.
Official religious law conflicts with equal standing across belief and with the secular republican model explicitly endorsed for Iran.
Civil policy should remain democratically accountable rather than require clerical approval.
Constitutional religious preference risks treating citizens outside the recognised faith as unequal members.
Religious literacy can support informed choice without state-directed conversion.
Cultivating an official faith constrains pupils’ independent development and privileges one belief.
Civil law and equal rights should govern public courts, including disputes involving religious customs.
An official clerical review role gives a religious group unequal power over other citizens’ laws.
Civic ceremonies should welcome citizens equally rather than organise worship on the state’s behalf.
Funding intended specifically to strengthen faith privileges a substantive religious life over others.
Government endorsement of a religious symbol is different from protecting citizens’ private expression.
A shared holiday may be convenient, but official recognition of the predominant faith gives it unequal governmental standing.
Public office should derive from equal civic institutions, not an inherited entitlement of religious leadership.
Charitable exemptions can be equal; additional exemptions solely for religious activity create a privilege without an equality justification.
Civil marriage and bodily autonomy should not depend on approval by religious authorities.
Binding religious family-law authority can constrain exit and equal rights, even where voluntary spiritual advice remains protected.

axes.brief: The selected egalitarian strand seeks to change gender roles and exclusionary institutions; contemporary NOW includes LGBTQIA+ equality and reproductive freedom.
axes.counterEvidence: Voluntarily chosen traditional lives remain possible. The profile rejects compulsory social hierarchy, not the worth of individual caregivers or every inherited custom.

answers.rationale: Re-examining institutions and customs is central to removing entrenched barriers to equality.
Tradition cannot take automatic priority over equal autonomy and changed needs.
Equal recognition should extend to diverse families rather than attach status to a single prescribed form.
The founding statement directly rejects assigning breadwinning and caregiving duties by sex.
Equal LGBTQIA+ civil rights support marriage on equal terms irrespective of partners’ sex.
State and social respect should support caring relationships without designating one family form inherently superior.
Reproductive freedom includes treating an early abortion as a legitimate personal decision.
Children’s autonomy and access to sex education limit a parental veto based on traditional sexual expectations.
Equal treatment of same-sex couples supports equal acceptance in parenting, judged by care rather than orientation.
Dress should follow personal choice, not a socially imposed gendered modesty requirement.
Respecting varied gender identities supports revising language to recognise people on their own terms.
Inherited moral rules should be assessed for equality rather than passed on as an overriding duty.
Rejecting sex-assigned roles directly supports equal acceptance of adults pursuing nontraditional activities.
Gradualism is not intrinsically preferable when it prolongs barriers to equal participation.
Comprehensive sexuality education and LGBTQIA+ inclusion support teaching beyond traditional family assumptions.
A freely valued intergenerational custom may be retained, but historical continuity alone cannot require preserving restrictive practices.

axes.brief: Technological change can expand women’s options, as the founding statement’s discussion of automation recognises. Effective choice also requires informed consent, reliable evidence and attention to unequal harms.
axes.counterEvidence: No cited programme settles cultivated meat, brain enhancement or embryo editing. Their responses are conditional applications of bodily autonomy, non-domination and protection of future persons; they are not attributed policy announcements. Prioritising technology is not the same as using it exclusively; the climate-policy priority is therefore conditional.

answers.rationale: Potentially liberating benefits favour adoption, while poorly understood harms can undermine autonomy; the scale and reversibility of risk determine permission.
Trials can protect informed choice, but a universal demand for long-term evidence may block important autonomy-enhancing treatments.
Infrastructure can improve access and independence, while irreversible habitat loss can damage others’ opportunities; proportionality must decide.
Medical autonomy requires dependable safety information rather than exposing patients broadly to inadequately studied lasting harms.
The founding analysis treats automation as an opportunity; adoption is supportable with retraining and equal access to its benefits.
Habitat protection and substantial social benefits both matter; neither receives unconditional priority from an equal-opportunity framework.
Cultivated meat may reduce harm but may create uncertain risks; controlled introduction and evidence determine support.
Irreversible enhancement with uncertain safety threatens informed autonomous choice, making a research-stage restriction defensible.
Technological solutions and reduced resource consumption can both preserve opportunities; the autonomy framework does not establish a general priority between them under uncertain scale.
Investigating poorly understood environmental effects before construction protects affected people’s ability to assess lasting consequences.
Competent adults have a strong choice interest, but basic safety alone may not disclose lasting neural risks; consent quality and reversibility decide.
Reliability across patient groups is crucial to equal healthcare and prevents discrimination hidden within diagnostic systems.
Research can expand future options, but inheritable enhancement raises non-consenting future persons’ interests; safeguards and scope determine acceptability.
Evidence about lasting ecosystem effects protects shared conditions of opportunity rather than treating early yields as sufficient.
Housing and accessible transport directly support economic independence, giving development weight when harms can be proportionately limited.
A credible risk of irreversible harm justifies stronger evidence because later choices cannot fully repair it.

axes.brief: National constitutional equality and enforceable labour and reproductive rights limit local exclusion. Local participation remains valuable within those guarantees (now; fem; resolutions).
axes.counterEvidence: Federal protection is not unlimited national executive discretion. Separate institutions, judicial review and meaningful community participation remain part of the liberal framework.

answers.rationale: Protected regional self-government can extend participation, provided constitutionally equal rights still bind the region.
A constitutional jurisdictional dispute should receive independent adjudication rather than the national government’s unilateral final word.
Self-determination supports a voice in secession, while affected minorities and reciprocal obligations require more than an unqualified majority rule.
Regional obstruction should not defeat nationwide equal-rights and care guarantees merely because it is locally popular.
Regional constitutions within national rights can provide legitimate local political autonomy.
National standards and local responsiveness both aid accountable policing; institutional scale alone does not prevent abuse.
Keeping most revenue locally can entrench unequal opportunities between rich and poor regions.
Common equality and educational access standards are justified, while local curricular choice can remain meaningful; total national control goes further.
Regional taxation can coexist with national redistribution and common rights, allowing accountable local choices.
National employment guarantees prevent local rules from undermining equal pay, leave and basic worker protection.
Local democratic control of council design supports political agency within constitutional rights and fair boundaries.
A national entitlement to reproductive and other essential care should not depend on regional political restrictions.
Indigenous local institutions can support equal collective participation, subject to individual civil rights and meaningful exit.
Limits on tax competition can protect funding needed for equal opportunities across regions.
Decisions with genuinely local effects can remain locally accountable without undermining national equality guarantees.
Cross-regional coordination can protect people effectively during a shared emergency while remaining democratically accountable.

axes.brief: NOW’s foundational analysis attributes constrained opportunities and sex roles substantially to education, institutions and expectations, while recognising biological childbearing. This is a social explanation of gender hierarchy, not a universal genetics theory.
axes.counterEvidence: Equal moral standing does not establish the heritability of stress, attention, temperament or group differences. Conditional neutrals express a mixed developmental model without declaring racial categories a valid biological hierarchy. The social explanation of gender roles is stronger than the evidence for specific unrelated causal comparisons; no political doctrine is presented as scientific proof.

answers.rationale: The tradition’s explanation of restricted choices gives upbringing and institutions more explanatory weight in ordinary social behaviour.

Equal educational opportunity is a normative commitment, not proof of the relative causes of international IQ differences; the representative model permits developmental and inherited contributions without ranking them here.
The critique of assigned sex roles explains much observed gender behaviour through expectations, training and constraints.
Embodied vulnerability and lived conditions can both shape stress; this representative model does not rank their contributions universally.
Education, encouragement and access shape the interests people can realistically develop, rather than reflecting fixed assigned roles.
Risk choices can involve dispositions as well as social incentives; autonomy theory supports neither universal causal ranking.
The account of reciprocal family relations treats cooperative habits as substantially cultivated by social arrangements.
Caregiving expectations influence empathy while individuals differ; the doctrine permits both developmental and dispositional contributions.
Attention can be affected by conditions of learning and embodied capacities; equal opportunity does not require one to dominate universally.
The analysis of internalised gender norms gives social learning substantial weight in immediate moral reactions.
Experiences of coercion and vulnerability provide a social explanation of what people learn to perceive as threatening.
Recognition of individual differences and socially developed agency supports interaction rather than a blanket temperament hierarchy.
Criticism of media images and gender norms supports a substantial cultural role in learned attractiveness preferences.

Opposition to racial hierarchy does not alone answer this comparative causal claim about violence; the model considers social conditions and human dispositions without treating racial categories as a validated biological explanation.
The focus on education and developable agency favours learned self-control over a fixed racial explanation, without claiming an empirical heritability finding.

NOW identifies occupational barriers, discrimination and the undervaluation of caregiving as causes of earnings differences. It therefore rejects explaining the gap through economic contribution instead of social expectations; this does not claim that every observed earnings difference has the same cause.

review.reviewer: Codex /root/libertarian_historical, separate evidence review of /root assessment
review.notes: Independently read all 240 literal questions and answer rationales, NOW founding statement, immigration principles, Core Issues and 2026 resolutions, SEP liberal-feminism analysis, and the Australian prime-ministerial June 2026 leave announcement. Confirmed the distinction between egalitarian and classical/libertarian feminisms and the role of NOW as one contemporary programme. Challenged ownership assumptions: housing equity does not establish public housing title; public care does not determine commercial privatisation; rail refers to infrastructure. Corrected the climate question’s priority-versus-exclusive distinction. Moderated universal permanent refugee admission because safe harbour alone does not entail permanence. Replaced unsupported comparative IQ/racial-violence causation with expressly mixed modelling, and moderated self-control inference. Other non-core neutral judgements were reviewed as conditional applications rather than missing answers. Contemporary Australian implementation is an illustrative policy instrument, not a claim that its government represents US feminism. No scores or answers were adjusted to evade similarity. Sources’ factual allegations in political resolutions are used to establish NOW positions, not independently adjudicated as true.

similarity.reason: Reviewed revision 1 of both profiles after independent literal-question and evidence checks. Retain both scoped subjects despite the diagnostic overlap: Scottish SNP civic nationalism centres national self-determination and residence-based membership, whereas US egalitarian liberal feminism centres gendered autonomy, equal political agency and reform of care institutions. The current questions capture much shared liberal and social-democratic policy, so similar coordinates do not establish doctrinal identity. Ownership, military, fiscal and secession responses retain evidence-based distinctions; source-supported values were not tuned to create distance. This decision is a named scope-retention judgement, not a claim that all civic nationalists or feminists share either profile.
